info.title: Iminify API
info.summary: Compress, convert and resize images, and scan web pages for every image they load.
info.description: Everything the Iminify website does with images, over HTTP. Every request carries a personal access token from Settings > API Tokens as a Bearer token, for an account whose email is verified. Compressions and page scans run in the background: create one, then poll it until it has finished, or on a paid plan have it sent to your server as a signed webhook when it does (https://www.iminify.com/docs/webhooks). The guides are at https://www.iminify.com/docs.

tags.name: Images
tags.description: Compress, convert and resize images, then download, rename, share or run them again.

tags.name: Upload groups
tags.description: One image and every size and format made from it, counted as one image: for a site or an app that keeps several sizes of each upload.

tags.name: Page scans
tags.description: Scan a web page for every image it loads and compress them all at once.

tags.name: Site crawls
tags.description: Crawl several pages of one site at once, from its sitemap or a list, with one report and one zip for the whole site.

tags.name: Weekly site checks
tags.description: Have a site you crawled crawled again every week, compressing only the images that are new or changed, with an email when a check finds some.

post.description:
Send the image itself as a multipart `file`, or its address as `url` and Iminify fetches it. The answer comes straight back with the status `queued` and a `Location` header; the compression runs in the background, usually for a few seconds, so poll the image until its status is `completed`, `already-optimized`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Each image counts one against your daily images and your compressions a minute, whether it came through here or through the website.

The file goes through the same checks as an upload on the website: a format Iminify reads (PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, GIF, HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, TIF), your plan's file size, a name of at most 128 bytes, and at most 64 megapixels, before and after any resize. An animated WebP or PNG can't be resized: with `width`, `height` or `scale` it is refused with `animation_not_resizable`, and one sent without them, in its own format, comes back with every frame. An address has to be public `http` or `https`: Iminify fetches it from its own servers, refuses private networks on the address and on every redirect, follows up to five redirects and gives up after 30 seconds. A file larger than your plan's size is refused, and Iminify keeps no more of it than that size. The file is named after the address. Iminify fetches up to 2 addresses for you at a time; one more sent before those finish is refused with `rate_limited`.

schema.description: The image, as a file or as the address to fetch it from, and the settings to compress it with.

url.description: The public address of the image to fetch. Send either this or `file`.

folder.description: The folder the image belongs in, like `holiday/beach`, so a zip of several images (`POST /images/download`) puts it there. Either slash separates folders, and characters a file name can't hold become a hyphen. Keeping folders comes with a paid plan; sent on another plan, the image is refused with `pro_required`.

ephemeral.description: Delete the image once you've saved it, for a caller that keeps its own copy. Send `DELETE /images/{id}` once you've written the result; anything you leave is deleted for you about 24 hours after the image finished, its files with it. Off by default, which keeps the image until you delete it. See [Deleting images once saved](/docs/images#deleting-images-once-saved).

priority.description: `background` for bulk work nobody waits on, such as a whole library: it runs after every image sent without it, on every plan, and counts against your limits the same. See [Bulk work](/docs/images#bulk-work).

level.description: How hard to compress. `smart` finds the lowest quality that still looks like your upload, `ultra` goes further and softens fine texture a little, `lossless` changes no pixel unless a `size_limit` needs it to, `none` only applies the format, the resize, the size limit and the metadata choice. See [Compression settings](/docs/compression-settings).

anyOf.description: Convert to this format. `auto` encodes the image in every format that can hold it and keeps the smallest. Leave it out to keep the upload's own format; a HEIC or TIFF always comes back in another one, because Iminify doesn't write either. `jpeg` is read as `jpg`.

keep_metadata.description: Keep the EXIF metadata (camera, date, location) in the optimized copy. Off by default, which strips it; the orientation is applied to the pixels first, so a photo never comes back on its side.

width.description: Resize to this width in pixels. Alone, the height follows the aspect ratio. With `height` too, the image is resized to exactly that size, and its proportions change if they differ. Up to 65535.

height.description: Resize to this height in pixels, the same way as `width`. Up to 65535.

scale.description: Resize to this percentage of the original, 1 to 100. Cannot be combined with `width` or `height`.

size_limit.description: The most the optimized copy may weigh, in kilobytes of 1,000 bytes, from 5 KB up. Iminify lowers the quality until the file fits, and makes the image smaller in pixels when the lowest quality is still over it. The limit comes before the level: under `lossless` or `none`, a file over it is encoded again with loss. A PNG or GIF kept in its own format that is over the limit comes back in a format with a quality to lower (JPG, WebP or AVIF), so `png` as the `format` is refused; an animation is never fitted. `size_limit_status` on the finished image says how it came out. See [Size limit](/docs/compression-settings#size-limit).

responsive_widths.description: Paid plans: also make the image at each of these widths in pixels, for an ``, like `[480, 768, 1200, 1600]`, the website's default. Up to 8 widths, each from 16 to 65535. Each width is made from the upload, at the same level and in the format the image is delivered in, and never enlarged: a width wider than the upload is made at the upload's own width, once. In a multipart form, repeat `responsive_widths[]` or send them in one field, separated by commas. They are made a few seconds after the image finishes; `responsive` on the image lists them. Sent on another plan, the image is refused with `pro_required`. See [Responsive sizes](/docs/images#responsive-sizes).

alt_text.description: Write an alt text and a suggested file name for the image with AI. On by default; send `false` to leave it out. A small copy of the image goes to Anthropic, whose Claude model writes both, and they arrive a few seconds after the image finishes. Each one counts against your daily AI alt texts; once those are used up the image still compresses, without one. See [Alt text and file names](/docs/images#alt-text-and-file-names).

alt_text_language.description: The language to write the alt text in, as one of these tags: `en` (English), `es` (Spanish), `fr` (French), `de` (German), `it` (Italian), `pt` (Portuguese), `nl` (Dutch), `pl` (Polish), `sv` (Swedish), `tr` (Turkish), `ru` (Russian), `uk` (Ukrainian), `ar` (Arabic), `fa` (Persian), `he` (Hebrew), `hi` (Hindi), `id` (Indonesian), `vi` (Vietnamese), `th` (Thai), `ja` (Japanese), `ko` (Korean), `zh-Hans` (Simplified Chinese), `zh-Hant` (Traditional Chinese). The suggested file name follows it when the language is written in the Latin alphabet, and is in English otherwise.

use_suggested_name.description: Rename the optimized copy to the suggested file name as soon as the alt text arrives, unless it already has a new name by then: yours, or an earlier suggestion.

post.description:
Opens the page in a browser on Iminify's servers, waits for it to load, scrolls to the bottom and collects every image it loaded, then compresses each one with the settings you send. It answers straight away with the status `queued`; a scan takes from a few seconds to a few minutes. Each scan counts one against your daily scans and your page scans a minute, and the images it finds don't count against your daily images. A scan stops at your plan's images per scan, skips SVG and AVIF files and anything over your plan's file size, and compresses an image that appears twice once.

The address can leave out `https://`. A page on a private network is refused. A page behind a login, or one that blocks automated browsers, usually comes back with no images, because the scanner sees what a signed-out visitor would.

source.description: Where each run gets its pages: `sitemap`, read again every week, or `pages`, the same list every week.

settings.description: The settings every image of every run is compressed with: the crawl's own.

height.description: The height every image is resized to, or `null`.

paused.description: `true` while the check does not run on your plan: your plan has no weekly site checks, or it checks fewer sites than you hold and this is not among your oldest. The check is kept and runs again once your plan covers it.

next_run_at.description: When the next run is due. A run starts soon after it, and while the check is paused it moves on a week at a time.

RecompressImageRequest.description: The settings to run the stored original through again with.

level.description: How hard to compress. `smart` finds the lowest quality that still looks like your upload, `ultra` goes further and softens fine texture a little, `lossless` changes no pixel unless a `size_limit` needs it to, `none` only applies the format, the resize, the size limit and the metadata choice. See [Compression settings](/docs/compression-settings).

anyOf.description: Convert to this format. `auto` encodes the image in every format that can hold it and keeps the smallest. Leave it out to keep the upload's own format; a HEIC or TIFF always comes back in another one, because Iminify doesn't write either. `jpeg` is read as `jpg`.

keep_metadata.description: Keep the EXIF metadata (camera, date, location) in the optimized copy. Off by default, which strips it; the orientation is applied to the pixels first, so a photo never comes back on its side.

width.description: Resize to this width in pixels. Alone, the height follows the aspect ratio. With `height` too, the image is resized to exactly that size, and its proportions change if they differ. Up to 65535.

height.description: Resize to this height in pixels, the same way as `width`. Up to 65535.

scale.description: Resize to this percentage of the original, 1 to 100. Cannot be combined with `width` or `height`.

size_limit.description: The most the optimized copy may weigh, in kilobytes of 1,000 bytes, from 5 KB up. Iminify lowers the quality until the file fits, and makes the image smaller in pixels when the lowest quality is still over it. The limit comes before the level: under `lossless` or `none`, a file over it is encoded again with loss. A PNG or GIF kept in its own format that is over the limit comes back in a format with a quality to lower (JPG, WebP or AVIF), so `png` as the `format` is refused; an animation is never fitted. `size_limit_status` on the finished image says how it came out. See [Size limit](/docs/compression-settings#size-limit).

responsive_widths.description: Paid plans: also make the image at each of these widths in pixels, for an ``, like `[480, 768, 1200, 1600]`, the website's default. Up to 8 widths, each from 16 to 65535. Each width is made from the upload, at the same level and in the format the image is delivered in, and never enlarged: a width wider than the upload is made at the upload's own width, once. In a multipart form, repeat `responsive_widths[]` or send them in one field, separated by commas. They are made a few seconds after the image finishes; `responsive` on the image lists them. Sent on another plan, the image is refused with `pro_required`. See [Responsive sizes](/docs/images#responsive-sizes).

alt_text.description: Write an alt text and a suggested file name for the image with AI. On by default; send `false` to leave it out. A small copy of the image goes to Anthropic, whose Claude model writes both, and they arrive a few seconds after the image finishes. Each one counts against your daily AI alt texts; once those are used up the image still compresses, without one. See [Alt text and file names](/docs/images#alt-text-and-file-names).

alt_text_language.description: The language to write the alt text in, as one of these tags: `en` (English), `es` (Spanish), `fr` (French), `de` (German), `it` (Italian), `pt` (Portuguese), `nl` (Dutch), `pl` (Polish), `sv` (Swedish), `tr` (Turkish), `ru` (Russian), `uk` (Ukrainian), `ar` (Arabic), `fa` (Persian), `he` (Hebrew), `hi` (Hindi), `id` (Indonesian), `vi` (Vietnamese), `th` (Thai), `ja` (Japanese), `ko` (Korean), `zh-Hans` (Simplified Chinese), `zh-Hant` (Traditional Chinese). The suggested file name follows it when the language is written in the Latin alphabet, and is in English otherwise.

use_suggested_name.description: Rename the optimized copy to the suggested file name as soon as the alt text arrives, unless it already has a new name by then: yours, or an earlier suggestion.

status.description: Where the scanner is. `queued`: waiting for the scanner. `scanning`: the page is open and its images are being collected. `completed`: images were found and queued. `no-image-found`: the page loaded but nothing on it could be compressed. `failed`: the page could not be scanned. `cancelled`: called off before it started. The images themselves keep compressing after `completed`; watch `images_in_progress`.

note.description: What the scanner wrote when it finished: how many images it found and what became of each, or why it failed. `null` until then.

settings.description: The settings every image the scan found is compressed with.

anyOf.description: The format every image is converted to, or `null` to keep each one's own.

scale.description: The percentage every image is scaled to, or `null`.

images_in_progress.description: How many of them are still queued or being compressed. The scan is done once its status has ended and this is 0.

images_finished.description: How many of them have finished.

original_size.description: Bytes of the finished images before compression.

optimized_size.description: Bytes of the same images after compression.

saved_percent.description: The same saving as a percentage, or `null` while no image has finished.

share_url.description: The page report's public link while it is shared, or `null`. The link answers only while your account is on a paid plan.

anyOf.description: Why it was skipped, the same codes as the scan's `skipped` list, or `null`.

image_id.description: The id of its compressed image, or `null`.

format_sizes.description: What the compressed file came to in each format, smallest first, when the scan's format was `auto` and more than one format was tried; otherwise `null`.

suggested_alt.description: An AI alt text for an image the page shows without one, written from its compressed copy, or `null`: the image has alt text, the scan was asked for none, it is still being written (the scan's `alt_texts_in_progress` counts it), the day's AI alt texts were used up, or the model gave no usable answer. sitemap.description: The address of the site's sitemap: an XML sitemap, a sitemap index or a text file with one address a line, gzipped or not. pages.description: The pages to crawl, all on one site (with or without `www.`), up to your plan's pages per crawl. `https://` can be left out of each, and an address listed twice is crawled once. A longer list is refused, not cut. Send this or `sitemap`, not both.

level.description: How hard to compress. `smart` finds the lowest quality that still looks like your upload, `ultra` goes further and softens fine texture a little, `lossless` changes no pixel unless a `size_limit` needs it to, `none` only applies the format, the resize, the size limit and the metadata choice. anyOf.description: Convert to this format. `auto` encodes the image in every format that can hold it and keeps the smallest. Leave it out to keep the upload's own format; a HEIC or TIFF always comes back in another one, because Iminify doesn't write either. `jpeg` is read as `jpg`.

keep_metadata.description: Keep the EXIF metadata (camera, date, location) in the optimized copy. Off by default, which strips it; the orientation is applied to the pixels first, so a photo never comes back on its side.

width.description: Resize to this width in pixels. Alone, the height follows the aspect ratio. With `height` too, the image is resized to exactly that size, and its proportions change if they differ. Up to 65535.

height.description: Resize to this height in pixels, the same way as `width`. Up to 65535.

scale.description: Resize to this percentage of the original, 1 to 100. Cannot be combined with `width` or `height`.

alt_text.description: Write an AI alt text for each image a page shows with no alt attribute at all, from its compressed copy, for that page's report (`suggested_alt` on its scan). On by default; send `false` to leave it out. Each one counts against your daily AI alt texts. See [Alt text and file names](/docs/images#alt-text-and-file-names).

StoreGroupRequest.description: The image a group stands for, as you will send it, and the outputs to make from it. Iminify makes every output itself from that one image, so you never send a size file. See [Upload groups](/docs/upload-groups).

name.description: The image's name, without its extension, like `IMG_2041`.

source.description: The image you will send as the group's source, described exactly: the upload is refused unless its format, its bytes and its width and height (as displayed, with its orientation applied) are these.

format.description: Its format: `jpg`, `png`, `webp` or `gif`. `jpeg` is read as `jpg`.

size.description: Its size in bytes, at most your plan's file size.

outputs.description: The outputs to make, the main one first: up to 30, each at most the source's width and height. The first output in the source's own format is the one an alt text is written for.

name.description: The output's name, like `thumbnail` or `medium_large`: letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores, up to 64, unique in the group whatever their case. It names the output's files, `thumbnail.webp` in the zip.

crop.description: Where to cut a cropped output, across then down: `start`, `center` or `end` each, like `["center", "center"]`. The source is scaled to cover the output, then cut at these anchors, as WordPress crops a size. Leave it out for an output that keeps the source's shape.

size.description: The bytes of the copy of this output you already have, if any. A file made for the output replaces your copy only when it is smaller.

formats.description: The formats to make each output in: `original` is the source's own, `webp` and `avif` a copy beside it. A WebP source's `webp` is its own format, made once. Leave it out for `original` alone.

level.description: How hard to compress every output. `smart` finds the lowest quality that still looks like the source, `ultra` goes further and softens fine texture a little, `lossless` changes no pixel, `none` only resizes, crops and converts. See [Compression settings](/docs/compression-settings).

keep_metadata.description: Keep the EXIF metadata (camera, date, location) in the outputs. Off by default, which strips it; the orientation is applied to the pixels first.

alt_text.description: Write an AI alt text and a suggested file name for the main output once the source arrives. Off by default for a group. A small copy of the image goes to Anthropic, whose Claude model writes both; it counts one against your daily AI alt texts, and once those are used up the group still runs, without one. See [Alt text and file names](/docs/images#alt-text-and-file-names).

alt_text_language.description: The language to write the alt text in, as one of these tags: `en` (English), `es` (Spanish), `fr` (French), `de` (German), `it` (Italian), `pt` (Portuguese), `nl` (Dutch), `pl` (Polish), `sv` (Swedish), `tr` (Turkish), `ru` (Russian), `uk` (Ukrainian), `ar` (Arabic), `fa` (Persian), `he` (Hebrew), `hi` (Hindi), `id` (Indonesian), `vi` (Vietnamese), `th` (Thai), `ja` (Japanese), `ko` (Korean), `zh-Hans` (Simplified Chinese), `zh-Hant` (Traditional Chinese). The suggested file name follows it when the language is written in the Latin alphabet, and is in English otherwise.

ephemeral.description: Delete the group once you've saved its files, for a caller that keeps its own copies. Send `DELETE /groups/{id}` once you've written them; a group you leave is deleted for you about 24 hours after its last file finished, its files and its source with it. Off by default, which keeps the group until you delete it. See [Deleting images once saved](/docs/images#deleting-images-once-saved).

See [Compression settings](/docs/compression-settings).

anyOf.description: Convert to this format. `auto` encodes the image in every format that can hold it and keeps the smallest. Leave it out to keep the upload's own format; a HEIC or TIFF always comes back in another one, because Iminify doesn't write either. `jpeg` is read as `jpg`.

keep_metadata.description: Keep the EXIF metadata (camera, date, location) in the optimized copy. Off by default, which strips it; the orientation is applied to the pixels first, so a photo never comes back on its side.

width.description: Resize to this width in pixels. Alone, the height follows the aspect ratio. With `height` too, the image is resized to exactly that size, and its proportions change if they differ. Up to 65535.

height.description: Resize to this height in pixels, the same way as `width`. Up to 65535.

scale.description: Resize to this percentage of the original, 1 to 100. Cannot be combined with `width` or `height`.

size_limit.description: The most the optimized copy may weigh, in kilobytes of 1,000 bytes, from 5 KB up. Iminify lowers the quality until the file fits, and makes the image smaller in pixels when the lowest quality is still over it. The limit comes before the level: under `lossless` or `none`, a file over it is encoded again with loss. A PNG or GIF kept in its own format that is over the limit comes back in a format with a quality to lower (JPG, WebP or AVIF), so `png` as the `format` is refused; an animation is never fitted. `size_limit_status` on the finished image says how it came out. See [Size limit](/docs/compression-settings#size-limit).

responsive_widths.description: Paid plans: also make the image at each of these widths in pixels, for an ``, like `[480, 768, 1200, 1600]`, the website's default. Up to 8 widths, each from 16 to 65535. Each width is made from the upload, at the same level and in the format the image is delivered in, and never enlarged: a width wider than the upload is made at the upload's own width, once. In a multipart form, repeat `responsive_widths[]` or send them in one field, separated by commas. They are made a few seconds after the image finishes; `responsive` on the image lists them. Sent on another plan, the image is refused with `pro_required`. See [Responsive sizes](/docs/images#responsive-sizes).

alt_text.description: Write an alt text and a suggested file name for the image with AI. On by default; send `false` to leave it out. A small copy of the image goes to Anthropic, whose Claude model writes both, and they arrive a few seconds after the image finishes. Each one counts against your daily AI alt texts; once those are used up the image still compresses, without one. See [Alt text and file names](/docs/images#alt-text-and-file-names).

alt_text_language.description: The language to write the alt text in, as one of these tags: `en` (English), `es` (Spanish), `fr` (French), `de` (German), `it` (Italian), `pt` (Portuguese), `nl` (Dutch), `pl` (Polish), `sv` (Swedish), `tr` (Turkish), `ru` (Russian), `uk` (Ukrainian), `ar` (Arabic), `fa` (Persian), `he` (Hebrew), `hi` (Hindi), `id` (Indonesian), `vi` (Vietnamese), `th` (Thai), `ja` (Japanese), `ko` (Korean), `zh-Hans` (Simplified Chinese), `zh-Hant` (Traditional Chinese). The suggested file name follows it when the language is written in the Latin alphabet, and is in English otherwise.

use_suggested_name.description: Rename the optimized copy to the suggested file name as soon as the alt text arrives, unless it already has a new name by then: yours, or an earlier suggestion.
